output.summary: Reviewed the single added file examples/acceptance/bounds.mjs. The bounds check has an off-by-one error: it uses `index > values.length` instead of `index >= values.length`, so the documented contract to throw RangeError for out-of-bounds indices is violated when index equals values.length (which returns undefined rather than throwing).

findings.title: Off-by-one bounds check allows index equal to values.length
findings.body: The guard `!Number.isInteger(index) || index < 0 || index > values.length` does not reject `index === values.length`. Because valid array indices range from 0 to `values.length - 1`, an index equal to `values.length` is out of bounds, yet the function reaches `return values[index]` and returns `undefined` instead of throwing RangeError, contradicting the docstring contract "throw RangeError outside the array".
findings.evidence: For index === values.length, the condition `index > values.length` is false, so `values[values.length]` evaluates to undefined rather than throwing RangeError.
findings.suggestion: Change the comparison to `index >= values.length` so all out-of-bounds indices, including index === values.length, throw RangeError.

output.diagnosis: The bounds predicate uses a strict `>` comparison against `values.length` instead of `>=`, leaving the boundary value `index === values.length` unguarded and returning undefined from `values[index]` rather than raising RangeError as required by the function contract.
